note: A live end-to-end build: the requirements panel, then every build stage, on real models. All text was written by models.
brief: Work out the billable hours for a hospital observation stay. Hours are the real time that passed between admission and discharge, both given as local times in the hospital's time zone, America/New_York. Round up to whole hours. Observation is billed for at most 48 hours.
facts: Made-up examples: admitted 2026-01-10 08:00, discharged 2026-01-10 10:01 is 3 hours. Admitted 2026-03-07 22:00, discharged 2026-03-08 22:00 is 23 hours, because the clocks went forward that night. Admitted 2026-10-31 22:00, discharged 2026-11-01 22:00 is 25 hours, because the clocks went back. Admitted 2026-01-10 08:00, discharged 2026-01-13 08:00 is billed as 48. All data is made up.

route.text:
How risky is this change?  → medium · 0.51  (low 0.01 · medium 0.51 · high 0.48)

Decision: the full panel. Two independent models check each other, and a person signs off at every gate.
A low-risk request, such as fixing a typo, would go to one model and a person, at a fraction of the cost.

panel.draftA:
REQ-1: Accept admission and discharge as local date-times in America/New_York. Convert each to an absolute instant using that zone's daylight saving rules before doing any arithmetic.
REQ-2: Elapsed time is discharge minus admission in real time, not wall-clock difference. Any partial hour rounds up to the next whole hour. An exact whole number of hours stays unchanged.
REQ-3: Billable hours = min(rounded elapsed hours, 48).
REQ-4: Reject a discharge earlier than admission. The brief does not cover local times that occur twice (e.g. 2026-11-01 01:30) or do not exist (e.g. 2026-03-08 02:30). The requester must decide how to handle them before build; until then, flag them rather than guess.
AC-1: Admitted 2026-01-10 08:00, discharged 2026-01-10 10:01. Elapsed is 2 h 1 min, which rounds up to 3 billable hours.
AC-2: Admitted 2026-03-07 22:00, discharged 2026-03-08 22:00. This gives 23 billable hours, because clocks went forward on Sunday 2026-03-08 (second Sunday of March, verified).
AC-3: Admitted 2026-10-31 22:00, discharged 2026-11-01 22:00. This gives 25 billable hours, because clocks went back on Sunday 2026-11-01 (first Sunday of November, verified).
AC-4: Admitted 2026-01-10 08:00, discharged 2026-01-13 08:00. Elapsed is 72 real hours, capped and billed as 48.

reviewOfA.strengths: Every acceptance figure matches real America/New_York elapsed time: 2 hours 1 minute ceilings to 3, the March 8 2026 spring-forward night is 23 hours, the November 1 2026 fall-back night is 25 hours, and 72 hours is capped at 48.

merge.document:
REQ-1: Accept admission and discharge as local date-times in America/New_York. Convert each to an absolute instant using that zone's daylight saving rules before doing any arithmetic.
REQ-2: Elapsed time is discharge minus admission in real time, not the wall-clock difference. Any partial hour rounds up to the next whole hour. An exact whole number of hours stays unchanged.
REQ-3: Billable hours = min(rounded elapsed hours, 48).
REQ-4: Some local times occur twice or not at all. On 2026-11-01, 01:00 to 01:59 occurs twice. On 2026-03-08, 02:00 to 02:59 does not exist. The brief does not say how to handle these, so elapsed hours for such stays are undefined. The requester must decide before build. Until then, the system flags these inputs and does not guess.
REQ-5: A discharge earlier than admission is flagged as invalid. The brief does not cover this case, so the requester should confirm it.
AC-1: Admitted 2026-01-10 08:00, discharged 2026-01-10 10:01. Elapsed time is 2 h 1 min, which rounds up to 3 billable hours.
AC-2: Admitted 2026-03-07 22:00, discharged 2026-03-08 22:00. Elapsed time is 23 h, so 23 billable hours. The clocks went forward on Sunday 2026-03-08, the second Sunday of March.
AC-3: Admitted 2026-10-31 22:00, discharged 2026-11-01 22:00. Elapsed time is 25 h, so 25 billable hours. The clocks went back on Sunday 2026-11-01, the first Sunday of November.
AC-4: Admitted 2026-01-10 08:00, discharged 2026-01-13 08:00. Elapsed time is 72 real hours, which is capped and billed as 48.
AC-5: An input with an ambiguous local time such as 2026-11-01 01:30, or a nonexistent one such as 2026-03-08 02:30, is flagged and no hours are computed.
merge.keptFromA: I kept draft A's structure: explicit conversion to absolute instants, the min() cap formula, the handling of ambiguous and nonexistent times, and acceptance criteria that show the elapsed-time working and the verified DST dates.

build.contract: billableObservationHours(input) where input = { admission, discharge } (strings, local date-times in America/New_York in the form "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm", e.g. "2026-03-07 22:00"). Returns { status: "ok" | "ambiguous" | "nonexistent" | "invalid", elapsedMinutes: number | null (whole real minutes; null unless status is "ok"), roundedHours: number | null (whole hours before the cap; null unless status is "ok"), billableHours: number | null (whole hours after the cap; null unless status is "ok"), flags: string[] (plain-words reasons naming the offending field; empty when status is "ok") }. Throws an Error whose message is "unknown field: <name>" if input has any other field.

architecture.draft:
1. Component: one pure function, billableObservationHours(input), in a new module. No I/O, no clock reads, no new dependencies. It uses the built-in Intl.DateTimeFormat with timeZone America/New_York.
2. Validate first: any key other than admission or discharge throws Error("unknown field: <name>"). A missing field, or a string not matching YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm as a real calendar date-time, returns status invalid with a flag naming the field.
3. Resolve each local time (REQ-1): build the two candidate instants at UTC-05:00 and UTC-04:00, then format each back in America/New_York. Count the candidates that reproduce the input. 1 match is ok, 2 is ambiguous (e.g. 2026-11-01 01:30), 0 is nonexistent (e.g. 2026-03-08 02:30) (REQ-4, AC-5).
4. Status precedence when the fields disagree: invalid, then nonexistent, then ambiguous. Every offending field is still listed in flags. For non-ok results, elapsedMinutes, roundedHours and billableHours are all null.
5. Arithmetic (REQ-2, REQ-3, REQ-5): elapsedMinutes = (discharge instant - admission instant) / 60000. If negative, return invalid and flag discharge. Otherwise roundedHours = ceil(elapsedMinutes / 60) and billableHours = min(roundedHours, 48). Equal times give 0; the requester should confirm this.
6. Data: input is { admission, discharge } as strings. Output is { status, elapsedMinutes, roundedHours, billableHours, flags }, exactly as in the contract. No persistence.
7. Hand-checked expectations for tests. AC-1: 121 min gives 3. AC-2: 1380 min gives 23 (2026-03-08 is the second Sunday of March). AC-3: 1500 min gives 25 (2026-11-01 is the first Sunday of November). AC-4: 4320 min gives roundedHours 72 and billableHours 48. Also cover 2026-11-01 01:30 as ambiguous, 2026-03-08 02:30 as nonexistent, reversed times, an extra field, and a malformed date.
8. File fence, the only files that may change: src/billing/observationHours.js (new) and test/billing/observationHours.test.js (new).
9. Out of fence: no edits to any other file, package manifest or lockfile.
10. Open for the requester: resolution of ambiguous and nonexistent times (REQ-4), the reversed-times rule (REQ-5), and the zero-length stay.
architecture.review:
No defects found.
Strengths: DST is applied before arithmetic via offset candidates checked with America/New_York, and the test figures match the rules: 121 minutes rounds to 3, spring-forward is 1380 minutes (23), fall-back is 1500 minutes (25), and 72 hours caps at 48.

6. Data: input is { admission, discharge } as strings. Output is { status, elapsedMinutes, roundedHours, billableHours, flags }, exactly as in the contract. No persistence.

code.summary:
The module is one expression that returns { billableObservationHours }.

How it works:
1. It throws "unknown field: <name>" for any key other than admission or discharge.
2. It checks each field strictly against YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm and requires a real calendar date, so 2026-02-30 is rejected.
3. For each local time it builds two candidate instants, one at UTC-05:00 and one at UTC-04:00. It formats each back in America/New_York using Intl with hourCycle h23. If both match, the time is ambiguous. If neither matches, it is nonexistent.
4. When the fields disagree, status precedence is invalid, then nonexistent, then ambiguous. All offending fields are listed in flags. Every numeric field is null for non-ok results.
5. A negative elapsed time returns invalid with a flag on discharge.
6. Otherwise roundedHours = ceil(minutes / 60) and billableHours = min(roundedHours, 48).

Results I worked out by tracing the code, not by running it:
- AC-1: 121 min, 3 hours.
- AC-2: 1380 min, 23 hours. Clocks go forward at 07:00Z on 2026-03-08.
- AC-3: 1500 min, 25 hours. Clocks go back at 06:00Z on 2026-11-01.
- AC-4: 4320 min, rounded 72, billed 48.
- 2026-11-01 01:30 is ambiguous: both 05:30Z and 06:30Z show 01:30 local.
- 2026-03-08 02:30 is nonexistent: 07:30Z shows 03:30 and 06:30Z shows 01:30.
- Equal times give 0 hours.

Open for the requester: how to resolve ambiguous and nonexistent times, whether reversed times should be invalid, and whether a zero-length stay should bill 0.
code.review:
No defects found.
Strengths: Resolves America/New_York local times to absolute instants with both DST offsets, so partial hours round up, exact hours stay put, and the 48-hour cap matches the spring-forward and fall-back examples without guessing ambiguous times.
code.resolutions: No defects found; DST handling, round-up, and 48-hour cap are correct. applied: Independently verified: AC-1 121 min gives 3 h; AC-2 03:00Z Mar 8 to 02:00Z Mar 9 is 23 h; AC-3 02:00Z Nov 1 to 03:00Z Nov 2 is 25 h; AC-4 72 h capped to 48; 2026-03-08 02:30 matches neither offset (nonexistent) and 2026-11-01 01:30 matches both (ambiguous). Reversed times flagged invalid. No code change needed.
